prompt: Validate IPv4 address text (four parts, 0-255 each, no stray leading zeros) and recognise the private ranges 10.x, 172.16-31.x and 192.168.x. Complete both methods in IpUtils, then run the tests.
explanation: Splitting on a literal dot needs the escaped regex "\\." because a bare dot matches any character, and passing -1 as the limit keeps trailing empty parts so "1.2.3." cannot sneak through as three parts. Each part is checked as text first -- digits only, no leading zero unless the part is exactly "0" -- and only then converted with Integer.parseInt for the 0-255 range test. isPrivate builds on isValidIPv4 rather than repeating the work, which is why an invalid address is never reported as private.
hints: text.split("\\.", -1) splits on a real dot and keeps empty pieces, so a trailing dot still shows up as a fourth empty part.
Reject a part that is empty, longer than three characters, or contains a non-digit BEFORE calling Integer.parseInt on it.
The leading-zero rule is: a part of length greater than 1 must not start with '0', which still allows the single character "0".
